senses.definition: to give someone or an institution official power, authority, or legal rights

examples.en: Executive authority is vested in the president.
examples.vi: Quyền hành pháp được trao cho tổng thống.

examples.en: The constitution vests parliament with the power to make laws.
examples.vi: Hiến pháp trao cho nghị viện quyền làm luật.

senses.vi: trao quyền; giao quyền; ban cho

senses.definition: to become fully owned by an employee, usually after a set period of employment

examples.en: Her stock options will vest over four years.
examples.vi: Quyền chọn cổ phiếu của cô ấy sẽ có hiệu lực trong bốn năm.

examples.en: The retirement benefits vest after ten years of service.
examples.vi: Quyền lợi hưu trí sẽ chính thức thuộc về bạn sau mười năm làm việc.

senses.vi: thuộc về; có hiệu lực; được trao quyền

thesaurus.definition: provide with power and authority
place (authority, property, or rights) in the control of a person or group of persons
become legally vested
clothe oneself in ecclesiastical garments
clothe formally; especially in ecclesiastical robes

vi_block: Giao cho, trao quyền cho; ban cho, phong.
Mặc áo quần cho; trang hoàng.
Thuộc về, đến với, rơi vào (quyền, tài sản... ).

wiktionary.gloss: To clothe with, or as with, a vestment, or garment; to dress; to robe; to cover, surround, or encompass closely.

examples: to vest a court with power to try cases of life and death
wiktionary.gloss: To clothe with authority, power, etc.; to put in possession; to invest; to furnish; to endow; followed by with and the thing conferred.

examples: The power of life and death is vested in the king, or in the courts.

, Book I
Empire and dominion […] was vested in him.
wiktionary.gloss: To place or give into the possession or discretion of some person or authority; to commit to another; with in before the possessor.

examples: to vest a person with an estate
an estate is vested in possession
wiktionary.gloss: To clothe with possession; also, to give a person an immediate fixed right of present or future enjoyment of.

examples: Upon the death of the Sovereign the Crown automatically vests in the next heir without the need of coronation or other formality.
wiktionary.gloss: (of an inheritance or a trust fund) To devolve upon the person currently entitled when a prior interest has ended.

examples: My pension vests at the end of the month and then I can take it with me when I quit.
wiktionary.gloss: To become vested, to become permanent.

idioms.gloss: In a reserved or secretive manner.
To devolve as matter of right without reference to immediate right of possession.
To do minimal work while waiting for one's stock options to vest.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English vecche, fecche, ficche, from Old Northern French veche, variant of Old French vece, from Latin vicia. Doublet of fitch.

thesaurus.definition: any of various climbing plants of the genus Vicia having pinnately compound leaves that terminate in tendrils and small variously colored flowers; includes valuable forage and soil-building plants

wiktionary.gloss: Any of several leguminous plants, of the genus Vicia, often grown as green manure and for their edible seeds.
Any of several similar plants within the subfamily Faboideae.
One who hunts waterfowl.

examples: The zoomorphic Hindu god Ganesha has the head of an elephant.
